notes: All 14 discovery/diamond candidates were independently considered, with the fee audit read for context. This file replaces only difficulty, metrics and audit notes; it makes no fee/route eligibility changes.

Four high bands are provisional agent judgments within public health: EID, Eurosurveillance, PHR and PCD from official acceptance summaries with the stated limitations. Ten remain unknown. General originality/quality screening alone is insufficient for a comparative band. No easy or moderate status is inferred from missing information, regional scope, citation impact or faster decisions.

Retrospective acceptance percentages, decision-year rates, typical annual summaries and published-article handling times have different populations. Exact source years are retained; null year means the source did not give a rate period. No historic or aggregate percentage is an individual manuscript acceptance probability.

Metrics are a bounded selection of official citation and editorial-performance disclosures, not an exhaustive indicator inventory. No third-party journal-directory values were used. OUP timing definitions were retrieved at https://academic.oup.com/pages/using-the-content/metrics ; both first/final decision measures include desk rejections.

Access is reported per record. Blocked pages and snippets are not presented as complete policy verification. Official editorial statements archived in PMC remain primary reporting, while PMC is the host rather than the journal publisher. Search results can reveal newer leads without establishing their complete contents.

Country, region, subject, article type, issue theme, data age and local-author conditions govern manuscript fit independently of fee route and difficulty. This is a catalog-level agent review, not manuscript matching or human scientific review.
